identityReview: Petr Pavel, born 1 November 1961 in Planá in then-Czechoslovakia, Czech president since the 9 March 2023 oath and retired army general. MA in international relations in 2006 is not a doctorate. Communist Party membership in 1985–1989 and intelligence training are documented without unsupported criminal implications. Chief of General Staff from 1 July 2012 to spring 2015; NATO Military Committee election on 20 September 2014, office from 26 June 2015 to June 2018. NATO chair, Secretary General and Supreme Allied Commander Europe are distinct offices. Direct presidential election victory on 28 January 2023 is separate from inauguration.
lifeStatusEvidence: Radiožurnál/iROZHLAS records his actual presence and interview on Národní třída on 17 November 2026. The presidential office independently records a completed meeting with the Hungarian president on 10 November. These are actual activities, not merely advance schedules; original audio and photographs were not inspected.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Czech presidential, defence ministry and NATO biographies; military history article; official election release and inauguration report; Czech public-broadcast accounts of the 2024 ammunition proposal, historical candidate profile and 2026 interview; and a dated presidential meeting release. Read Commons licence and crop history and a ČTK portrait-release report. No image pixels obtained.
corrections: Read the Czech presidential biography: born 1 November 1961 in Planá near Mariánské Lázně; military college graduation 1983, postgraduate intelligence study in Brno, and MA in international relations at King’s College London in 2006. It acknowledges Communist Party membership in 1985–1989 and entry to the General Staff intelligence administration in 1988. Its shorthand of NATO election in 2015 conflicts with the precise September 2014 election in NATO and defence records; the profile distinguishes election from June 2015 assumption of office. The rescue total of 53 differs from the Czech Radio profile’s 33, so no number is published. Its broad narrative ordering is not used to date the UNPROFOR rescue after the Belgian attaché post. The biography also supports the 2020 fundraising initiative and 6 September 2022 candidacy.

Read the defence ministry’s historical biography: military college 1979–1983, postgraduate study 1988–1991, British courses and King’s College study in 2005–2006. It dates chief-of-staff service to 1 July 2012–30 April 2015 and NATO election to 20 September 2014 in Vilnius. NATO prose says the national post ended in May 2015; the profile uses spring 2015 rather than pretending this precision difference is resolved. The ministry’s brigadier promotion date of 12 December 2002 differs from 1 December in other official biographies and is not used. Historical page headings do not establish a current military appointment.

Read NATO biography and service table: elected chair on 20 September 2014, took office on 26 June 2015, term June 2015–June 2018. The role is military advice and committee leadership, not NATO Secretary General or Supreme Allied Commander Europe. Birth and education corroborate presidential records. Its 1985–1991 company-command span is broader than the presidency’s 1985–1988 command plus 1988–1991 study sequence; no unsupported uninterrupted command claim is made. National military representation at US CENTCOM is not US military command. Login-interface text on the page did not block the public biography; no authentication was attempted.

Read Military History Institute Prague article of 26 April 2018: birth and military schooling, international-relations study, UNPROFOR operation in January 1993 to evacuate a French unit under fire, and subsequent French Croix de Guerre. It supports the event without supplying a disputed rescue total. It also confirms 2014 NATO election versus June 2015 assumption. Its description of a future June 2018 successor was a contemporary forecast, not evidence of 2026 office or activity.

Read Czech Statistical Office release of 28 January 2023: Pavel won the second round with 58.32% and Babiš received 41.67%; 5,759,197 valid votes and 70.25% turnout are separate quantities. The percentage refers to valid runoff votes, not all eligible voters, total population, the first round or parliamentary seats. The release said the electoral commission would meet on Monday; no same-day completion of that later approval is inferred. No ballot-level dataset or separate commission decision was inspected.

Read the government’s 9 March 2023 inauguration article, reached from its photo-gallery link: Pavel took the oath at a joint meeting of both parliamentary chambers in Vladislav Hall and succeeded Miloš Zeman. Election victory on 28 January is distinct from taking office on 9 March. Fiala’s positive assessment of the incoming president is political commentary, not independently measured presidential performance. Gallery captions were read, not original photographs.

Read ČT24/ČTK report of 17 February 2024 on the Munich Security Conference. Pavel identified possible procurement of 500,000 rounds of 155 mm and 300,000 rounds of 122 mm ammunition and sought partner financing. This was an availability and funding announcement, not proof all 800,000 rounds were delivered. The report attributes statements to Pavel and Defence Minister Černochová. No specific supplier countries, completed contract value, later delivery tally or independent audit is inferred from the announcement. Embedded videos were not viewed.

Read Czech Radio’s candidate profile, published 25 November 2022 and updated 14 January 2023. It corroborates birth, Communist Party membership in 1985–1989, intelligence training, retirement in 2018, the 2020 initiative and 6 September 2022 campaign announcement. His stated regret is attributed to him. The report mentions a negative lustration certificate; the original certificate and intelligence archives were not examined, and no criminal finding is inferred. Its rescued-soldier total of 33 conflicts with the presidency’s 53. Its January first-round result is not the eventual 58.32% runoff result. The site’s 2026 header date is not the article’s update date.

Read the 17 November 2026 Radiožurnál/iROZHLAS interview, published at 11:20, including the reported visit to Národní třída and his answers on domestic protest and government responsibility. It establishes actual public activity on the remembrance day. He expressly said he followed the earlier Letná demonstration at home; he is not recorded as attending that protest. Interviewer descriptions of protest size, political demands and planned international meetings are not independently certified outcomes. Original audio was not heard.

Read the presidential office release of 10 November 2026 confirming Pavel and Eva Pavlová welcomed Hungarian President András Baka and Katalin Kövesdi at Prague Castle. Discussed topics were nuclear energy, EU external borders and European industrial competitiveness. This supports a completed meeting, not a new binding treaty, completed project or independently demonstrated economic outcome. The 2026 counterpart names are taken from the dated release; no older officeholder is substituted.

additionalConsulted.access: Read English presidential CV. It explicitly distinguishes the 2014 NATO election and 2015–2018 chairmanship and describes military retirement in 2018. Broad career entries were cross-checked against the dated NATO and defence records.

Read ČTK report published 3 May 2023 describing the official portrait’s release, different background colors and a monochrome option. This does not independently prove the Commons candidate is a natural-color portrait.
Opening returned a recaptcha page. Search preview was not treated as a read article and supplies no published claim.

sourceReview.limits: AI editorial and translation review, not certified human or native-language review. Rescue total remains unresolved and is omitted. No personal degree certificates, original intelligence files or lustration certificate, full election audit, ammunition contracts or delivery audit, original interview audio, portrait pixels or private VRT correspondence examined. Current political assessments remain attributed and future plans are not completed results.

Original request returned curl exit 22, 403/HTTP000; no pixels obtained. Its size differs from the current original; source-to-crop relationship, identity, natural color, framing and sharpness require inspection.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages checked against the Chinese profile and English intermediary: 1 November 1961 birth in then-Czechoslovakia; 1979–1983 military study; 2006 MA; 1985–1989 party membership; 1983–2018 military service; January 1993 rescue without a disputed total; 1 July 2012 national military appointment; 20 September 2014 NATO election versus 26 June 2015 assumption and June 2018 end; 2020 fundraising; 6 September 2022 candidacy; 28 January 2023 runoff and 58.32% of valid votes versus 9 March oath; 17 February 2024 proposed 500,000 plus 300,000 rounds rather than completed delivery; actual 10 and 17 November 2026 activities without inferred Letná attendance.
